# Voice profile for Lumen Notes, inferred from the landing page (index.html).
#
#   kapi voice guide --profile-file voice.yaml            # render the guide
#   kapi voice check <file> --profile-file voice.yaml --json --min-score 80
#
# Terms are split deliberately:
#   forbidden_terms     — a clean 1:1 swap exists, so `kapi voice rewrite` can
#                         apply it safely, OR the word is banned outright with
#                         no replacement because the fix is to recast the
#                         sentence (an empty replacement means "flag, never
#                         auto-substitute").
#   prohibited_patterns — families of variants, and anything where a mechanical
#                         swap would produce nonsense.

name: Lumen Notes
description: >-
  The voice of Lumen Notes: calm, plainspoken and warm. It talks to one person
  who thinks on paper, promises less than it could, and stays out of the way —
  the way the product does.

tone:
  personality: [calm, plainspoken, warm, unhurried]
  formality: neutral
  emotion: warm
  humor: none
  guidelines: >-
    Address one reader as "you"; never "users". The product is a companion, not
    a platform — "notes that think with you", not a system you operate. Lead
    with what the reader gets to do, in a verb they would actually use ("jot it
    down", not "capture and organize your knowledge base"). Prefer a concrete
    specific over an intensifier: "the two-minute tour", not "a quick tour".
    Calm is the promise, so the sentence has to sound calm — no exclamation
    marks, no hype, nothing shouted. Be candid even when candour is an
    invitation to leave ("Leave whenever you like — no lock-in"). The assistant
    is described by what it does, never by the technology behind it.

style:
  active_voice: true
  sentence_length: varied
  person_pov: second
  contractions: sometimes
  prohibited_patterns:
    - regex: "\\w!($|[^=])"
      description: >-
        Exclamation marks in prose. The voice is calm, never excitable.
        Anchored to a word character so markup (<!doctype) and code (!=) are
        not flagged.
      severity: minor
    - regex: "(?i)\\b(revolutionary|game[- ]?changing|cutting[- ]?edge|world[- ]?class|next[- ]?gen(eration)?|best[- ]?in[- ]?class|enterprise[- ]grade)\\b"
      description: Hype adjectives. The page claims calm, not greatness.
      severity: major
    - regex: "(?i)\\b(synergy|synergies|empower(s|ed|ing)?)\\b"
      description: >-
        Corporate abstractions with no clean swap — recast the sentence around
        what the reader actually does.
      severity: minor
    - regex: "(?i)(ai[- ]powered|powered by ai|ai[- ]driven|our ai\\b)"
      description: >-
        The page describes what the assistant does and never names the
        technology. Say "the assistant" and recast the sentence around it.
      severity: major
    - regex: "(?i)\\b(supercharge|unlock your|10x|effortless(ly)?)\\b"
      description: Growth-marketing verbs. They break the unhurried register.
      severity: major

vocabulary:
  preferred_terms:
    - term: you
      note: Address one reader directly. The page never says "we" and never says "users".
    - term: the assistant
      note: How the AI feature is named. Never "AI", "AI-powered", or "our AI".
    - term: note
      note: The unit of content. Not "document", "entry", or "item".
    - term: Start free
      note: Short CTA wording, as in the nav. The long form is "Get started for free".
    - term: calm
      note: A brand word, used literally ("a calm, distraction-free editor").
    - term: no lock-in
      note: House phrasing for data portability. Pairs with "encrypted and exportable".

  forbidden_terms:
    # Safe 1:1 swaps — `kapi voice rewrite` can apply these unattended.
    - term: users
      replacement: you
      severity: minor
    - term: utilize
      replacement: use
      severity: minor
    - term: leverage
      replacement: use
      severity: minor
    - term: facilitate
      replacement: help
      severity: minor
    - term: commence
      replacement: start
      severity: minor
    # Banned outright, no auto-substitution: swapping a word here yields
    # nonsense ("our solution" -> "our Lumen Notes"). Recast the sentence.
    - term: seamless
      severity: major
    - term: seamlessly
      severity: major
    - term: robust
      severity: minor
    - term: powerful
      severity: minor
    - term: platform
      severity: minor
    - term: solution
      severity: minor

  competitor_terms: []   # none named on the landing page — needs your input

examples:
  - before: Leverage our AI-powered platform to maximize your note-taking productivity.
    after: Jot it down, and let the assistant connect the dots.
    explanation: >-
      Name what the assistant does, not the technology behind it. Lead with a
      verb the reader would actually use.
    category: vocabulary
  - before: Users can utilize our robust search functionality to locate previously created content.
    after: Full-text search across every note, so nothing you wrote is ever truly lost.
    explanation: >-
      Say "you", say it in plain words, and end on the reassurance that is the
      real point of the feature.
    category: style
  - before: Our seamless, distraction-free experience empowers you to unlock your best writing!
    after: A calm, distraction-free editor that stays out of your way so the words can flow.
    explanation: >-
      Cut the hype and the exclamation mark. Calm is the promise, so the
      sentence has to sound calm.
    category: tone
  - before: Enterprise-grade security and best-in-class data governance keep your content safe.
    after: Your notes are encrypted and exportable. Leave whenever you like — no lock-in.
    explanation: >-
      Concrete and checkable beats a grade. Say the plain thing, even when it is
      an invitation to leave.
    category: tone

runs.finalText:
Detected stack: Next.js 16.2 App Router, React 19, TypeScript, no i18n yet, and `src/app/page.tsx` is already `"use client"`. Two options are genuinely in play for you; the rest aren't.

| Option | Toil grade | What you sign up for |
|---|---|---|
| **@neokapi/i18n-react** | **T0** — add and forget | Plain JSX *is* the catalog; a webpack-hook plugin extracts at build time. No wrapping, no key hygiene. Runtime is client-side. |
| **next-intl** | T2 — standing chore | The App Router ecosystem standard. Best RSC/server-render ergonomics; you hand-author `messages/en.json` with dot-key IDs and own key hygiene forever. |

Lingui (T2) is the reasonable middle if you want source-as-key with a conventional library. **react-intl is T3** — maximum per-string boilerplate plus hash-ID churn on every copy edit; only correct if you have an existing FormatJS/ICU mandate and a TMS.

## The deciding question

Content context is set up and the ship gate is green.

## What's bound

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `kapi.yaml` | project `northwind`, source `en`, two collections: `product` → `README.md`, `marketing` → `marketing/**/*.docx` |
| `voice.yaml` | the house voice profile, bound via `defaults.voice.profile_file` |
| `.kapi/terms.json` | the terms store |
| `terms-seed.jsonl` | the change-set that produced the terms, kept as the reviewable record |

Every rule traces to a sentence you already wrote — `README.md` ("We write plainly and we do not shout") and `marketing/tone.md` ("plain words… no marketing superlatives… address the reader as you"). Nothing came from a generic B2B pack:

- **Tone** plain, direct, calm; neutral formality; no humor. **Style** active, short sentences, second person.

- **Forbidden terms** `utilize`→`use`, `leverage`→`use`, `facilitate`→`help`, `in order to`→`to`.
- **Examples** three before/after pairs built from your own README sentence.
- **`competitor_terms` is empty on purpose** — no competitor is named anywhere in the repo, and inventing one would gate your builds on a guess.

Contractions is set to `sometimes`, not `never`: both samples spell them out ("do not shout", "We will provision"), but two data points is thin evidence for a rule that fires on every draft. Tighten it if that's house style.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Parse application log files of the form:

    2026-08-01 12:00:00 INFO started

Prints matching entries, or a per-level summary with --summary.
"""

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from datetime import datetime

LINE_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<timestamp>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2})\s+"
    r"(?P<level>[A-Z]+)\s+"
    r"(?P<message>.*)$"
)

TIMESTAMP_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"


class ParseError(Exception):
    """A line that does not match the expected log format."""


def parse_line(line):
    """Parse one log line into a dict, or raise ParseError."""
    match = LINE_RE.match(line.rstrip("\n"))
    if not match:
        raise ParseError("does not match 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS LEVEL message'")
    fields = match.groupdict()
    fields["timestamp"] = datetime.strptime(fields["timestamp"], TIMESTAMP_FORMAT)
    return fields


def parse_file(path):
    """Yield (lineno, entry, error) for every non-blank line in path.

    Exactly one of entry/error is None.
    """
    stream = sys.stdin if path == "-" else open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    try:
        for lineno, line in enumerate(stream, start=1):
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            try:
                yield lineno, parse_line(line), None
            except ParseError as exc:
                yield lineno, None, str(exc)
    finally:
        if stream is not sys.stdin:
            stream.close()


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                     formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("files", nargs="+", help="log files to parse ('-' for stdin)")
    parser.add_argument("--level", action="append", metavar="LEVEL",
                        help="only show this level; repeatable (e.g. --level WARN --level ERROR)")
    parser.add_argument("--contains", metavar="TEXT",
                        help="only show entries whose message contains TEXT (case-insensitive)")
    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true",
                        help="emit one JSON object per entry instead of text")
    parser.add_argument("--summary", action="store_true",
                        help="print counts per level instead of entries")
    parser.add_argument("--strict", action="store_true",
                        help="exit non-zero if any line fails to parse")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    wanted = {lvl.upper() for lvl in args.level} if args.level else None
    needle = args.contains.lower() if args.contains else None

    counts = {}
    bad_lines = 0

    for path in args.files:
        try:
            lines = parse_file(path)
        except OSError as exc:
            print(f"{path}: {exc.strerror}", file=sys.stderr)
            bad_lines += 1
            continue

        for lineno, entry, error in lines:
            if error is not None:
                bad_lines += 1
                print(f"{path}:{lineno}: skipped, {error}", file=sys.stderr)
                continue

            if wanted is not None and entry["level"] not in wanted:
                continue
            if needle is not None and needle not in entry["message"].lower():
                continue

            counts[entry["level"]] = counts.get(entry["level"], 0) + 1
            if args.summary:
                continue

            if args.json:
                print(json.dumps({
                    "file": path,
                    "line": lineno,
                    "timestamp": entry["timestamp"].isoformat(),
                    "level": entry["level"],
                    "message": entry["message"],
                }))
            else:
                stamp = entry["timestamp"].strftime(TIMESTAMP_FORMAT)
                print(f"{path}:{lineno}\t{stamp}\t{entry['level']}\t{entry['message']}")

    if args.summary:
        total = sum(counts.values())
        for level, count in sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0])):
            print(f"{level:<8}{count}")
        print(f"{'TOTAL':<8}{total}")
        if bad_lines:
            print(f"{'SKIPPED':<8}{bad_lines}")

    return 1 if (args.strict and bad_lines) else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
